overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of why international coordination on AI is difficult. You'll be asked about summits and declarations, scientific and treaty bodies, security competition and export controls, and positions on military use and autonomous weapons.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: A news report says that dozens of countries "signed a declaration on AI" at a summit. What does that tell you about the signers' obligations?

options.html: They must change their national laws within a set period
options.text: They must change their national laws within a set period
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A declaration creates no legal duty. It records what governments were willing to say together.

options.html: They face penalties from the host country if they don't comply
options.text: They face penalties from the host country if they don't comply
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A host country has no power to penalize signers. A declaration creates no legal duty.

options.html: They have stated an intent and taken on no legal duty
options.text: They have stated an intent and taken on no legal duty
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A declaration is non-binding. It states what governments believe or intend, and nothing happens to a signatory that ignores it.

options.html: They have ratified a treaty that inspectors will monitor
options.text: They have ratified a treaty that inspectors will monitor
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Ratification applies to treaties. A declaration creates no legal duty and has no inspectors.

forms.stemHtml: What does the UN's Independent International Scientific Panel on AI produce?

options.html: An annual report assessing the evidence
options.text: An annual report assessing the evidence
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The panel produces evidence-based assessments of AI's opportunities, risks, and impacts. The UN says it won't set rules, enforce standards, or prescribe policy.

options.html: Binding safety standards for AI companies
options.text: Binding safety standards for AI companies
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The UN says the panel is not a regulatory body and won't set rules or enforce standards. It produces an annual report assessing the evidence.

options.html: Licenses for the export of advanced chips
options.text: Licenses for the export of advanced chips
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Export licenses are issued by national governments. The panel produces an annual report assessing the evidence.

options.html: Rulings on disputes between member states
options.text: Rulings on disputes between member states
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The panel isn't a court. It produces an annual report assessing the evidence.

forms.stemHtml: Two rival governments each believe advanced AI will bring a decisive advantage. According to the logic of an arms race, what would each need before accepting a limit on its own development?

options.html: Proof that AI brings no military advantage at all
options.text: Proof that AI brings no military advantage at all
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The race logic doesn't require that. Each side needs confidence that the other is keeping the same limit, which is a matter of verification.

options.html: A promise from its own AI companies to slow down
options.text: A promise from its own AI companies to slow down
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A domestic promise doesn't address the rival. Each side needs confidence that the other is keeping the same limit, which is a matter of verification.

options.html: A declaration signed by a majority of UN members
options.text: A declaration signed by a majority of UN members
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A declaration is non-binding and doesn't show what a rival is doing. Each side needs confidence that the other is keeping the same limit, which is a matter of verification.

options.html: Confidence that the rival keeps the same limit
options.text: Confidence that the rival keeps the same limit
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Neither side will hold back unless it can confirm the other is doing so too. That is why verification is central.

forms.stemHtml: Which of these did the 2021 Red Cross position and the 2023 joint call with the UN Secretary-General ask for? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Ruling out autonomous weapons whose effects can't be predicted
options.text: Ruling out autonomous weapons whose effects can't be predicted
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Both texts ask that unpredictable autonomous weapon systems be prohibited.

options.html: Ruling out the autonomous targeting of people
options.text: Ruling out the autonomous targeting of people
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The Red Cross position says use against human beings should be ruled out, and the joint call describes it as a moral line.

options.html: A ban on every military use of AI
options.text: A ban on every military use of AI
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Neither text asks for that. They ask to prohibit two categories of autonomous weapon and to restrict the others.

options.html: A legally binding instrument negotiated by states
options.text: A legally binding instrument negotiated by states
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The joint call asked world leaders to negotiate a new legally binding instrument and to conclude it by 2026.

forms.stemHtml: The US Defense Department's directive requires that autonomous weapon systems allow "appropriate levels of human judgment over the use of force." What does this standard permit?

options.html: Only weapons that a person fires by hand
options.text: Only weapons that a person fires by hand
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The directive permits autonomous weapons, after review and approval by senior officials. Judgment can be exercised before a system is activated.

options.html: Autonomous weapons, after senior review
options.text: Autonomous weapons, after senior review
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The directive permits autonomous weapons and requires senior officials to approve them. Human judgment can be exercised before activation, which differs from continuous human control.

options.html: Any weapon, with no review required
options.text: Any weapon, with no review required
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The directive requires senior officials to review and approve autonomous weapons before development and before fielding.

options.html: Only weapons that a treaty has approved
options.text: Only weapons that a treaty has approved
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. No treaty on autonomous weapons exists, and the directive is one country's internal policy. It permits autonomous weapons after review and approval by senior officials.

title: International coordination, security, and military use
